newsitem.title: USA: UP Resources cites Austin Chalk successes.
newsitem.headline: UP Resources cites Austin Chalk successes.

text.p: Union Pacific Resources Group Inc said Tuesday it is accelerating development activities in the Louisiana extension of the Austin Chalk as the result of encouraging tests from two new wells, the Crosby 8-1 and the Crosby 24-1, both located in Vernon Parish, La.

The results from these wells, combined with positive results of other operators in the Masters Creek area, have caused the company to propose a doubling of the Masters Creek Processing Plant's capacity to 200 million cubc feet a day, Union Pacific Resources said.
The plant's first l00 million cubic feet of capacity will be operating at full capacity upon completion in June, the company said.
The expansion proposal is pending board approval, spokesman Pat Doyle said.

The Crosby 8-1, in which UPR owns a 100 percent working interest, tested 22 million cubic feet of natural gas and 4,200 barrels of oil per day, at a flowing pressure of 7,500 pounds per square inch, the company said. The well was drilled to test the productive capability of some 50,000 acres where UPR has a 100 percent working interest.
The well is more than 10 miles from the nearest established production and significantly extends the productive limits of the prolific Masters Creek area.

Drilling has also been completed on the Crosby 24-1 in which UPR owns a 47.5 percent working interest. The other owners are Helmerich & Payne Inc, Occidental Petroleum Corp and the Royal Dutch/Shell Group Shell Oil Co subsidiary, Doyle said.
Early flow tests from this well indicate that it is another strong completion in the Masters Creek Field, where the Crosby 33-1 was completed in November 1996.

Since its completion, the 33-1 well has produced in excess of 1 billion cubic feet of natural gas and 285,000 barrels of crude oil. The well continues to produce at a rate of 13 million cubic feet of natural gas and 3,600 barrels of oil daily, Union Pacific Resources said.
It said final flow testing of the Crosby 24-1 will be completed in the next two weeks.
The company said its net production from the greater Masters Creek area is expected to exceed 75 million cubic feet of natural gas equivalent per day upon connection of the Crosby wells.

"The impressive success of the Crosby Wells has caused UPR to target an increase in its Louisiana Austin Chalk rig count from six to 12 which will allow us to drill 41 wells in 1997, while participating in 20 nonoperated wells," said Jack L. Messman, chief executive officer.
"Since UPR controls in excess of 575,000 net acres in the Louisiana extension of the Austin Chalk, we expect to be the significant player in this area for the foreseeable future."
